back: Defensive programming is a practice whereby the programmer tries to anticipate all of the ways the software could be misused, either by end-users, or by other developers (including the programmer themselves) using the code. These misuses can often be detected and then mitigated (e.g. by asking a user who entered bad input to try again).

For example, if you ask the user to enter an integer, and they enter a letter instead, how does your program behave in such a case? Unless you anticipated this, and added some error handling for this case, probably not very well.
